headline: Dry weather through Wednesday with morning fog and frost, then light rain chances return Thursday.
summary: High pressure over British Columbia, which usually means settled, dry air, and a storm system far to the south off California keep western Washington dry. A weather system approaching the coast late Sunday and Monday mostly heads toward California, so clouds thicken but little rain is expected here. Highs should reach the 50s to low 60s through Monday. Clear, light-wind nights bring morning fog Tuesday and Wednesday, plus some frost away from the water. Around Thursday, a weak dip in the upper-level winds, called a trough, brings a return of light rain chances into late next week. Temperatures stay near normal, warmest around midweek. Forecasters are fairly confident in the dry stretch, but the timing and amounts of late-week rain are uncertain.
